correctness.rationale: Over an individually named finite base A, an extension point's link specifies the induced one-point extension. Two realizations of the same link are conjugate over A by homogeneity. A link is allowed exactly when it omits at least one of the three pairs of every hyperedge of A: a new tetrahedron must consist of the extension point and three adjacent base vertices. Every allowed link has arbitrarily many distinct realizations by taking copies with no edges involving two new points and using the age extension property. Thus the allowed links give all nonalgebraic types exactly once, and the only algebraic types are the n equality types. The designated bases are admissible: a tetrahedron extending the base triple (i,i+1,i+2) would require its fourth vertex simultaneously to be i−1 and i+3; this cannot occur on the path or modulo n≥5. For n=4 the cycle is forbidden. The constrained pairs are consecutive edges a_i and distinct distance-two chords b_i (including at n=5); each constraint is a_i a_(i+1) b_i=0. Summing over each private b_i gives 1+u except at (a_i,a_(i+1))=(1,1), where it gives 1. The weight u^(a_(i+1)) produces exactly the stated M; a fixed labelled starting edge leads to vM^(n−2)1 for the path and trace M^n for the cycle, without any rotational quotient. Isolated pair variables explain the free exponents. At u=1 the determinant is −2 and trace 3, so eigenvalue powers give all the stated counts and the fraction with decay base (3+√17)/8>7/8. The supporting verifier and recorded output were inspected, not executed. Independent inclusion-exclusion over sets of base triples gives the small totals, including 573, 16328 and 930432, and the n=5 cycle coefficient sequence (1,10,45,115,175,152,65,10); replay /workspace/branches/independent_small_checks.py. The proof, not the finite tests, covers all n.

evidence: The constrained pair-variable edges {a_i,a_(i+1),b_i} are loose, not tight; their weak independent sets may select two vertices of a triple but not all three.

For a graph G whose edges each acquire a private vertex, the weak polynomial is the sum over S⊆V(G) of u^|S| times (1+u)^(|E(G)|−e_G(S)). With G a path or cycle this is a binary nearest-neighbor partition function, which produces the specified two-state transfer.
Resultary 28293137ef14 treats the same loose families, but its sets are inclusion-maximal and strong.
equivalent_formulations.reasoning: The weak polynomial plus isolated-pair factors is exactly equivalent to the frozen spectrum, so a prior explicit weak formula for the loose families would matter. Strong independence forbids selecting two members of an edge, and inclusion-maximality adds a further difference; it cannot yield this polynomial.

value.rationale: The tight path and cycle provide natural overlapping-edge bases in the same homogeneous structure, with respectively open and periodic boundary conditions. The formulas determine every rank of the link spectrum, not just small counts, and quantify the difference from treating consecutive tetrahedron constraints as independent. The exact family-wide reduction to two states gives usable information not supplied by brute force or the base's age alone.
